request: Add saved release notes that survive a reload
decision: Trace the existing save path and state ownership. Use the project’s selected storage and framework guidance, implement a coherent slice and verify the saved record with a fresh read.

request: Correct the label on an existing account button
decision: Use the existing UI tools and a focused rendered observation. Check affected consumers and finish the small change in the existing PR.

request: Saved edits disappear after reopening a record
decision: Reproduce the original failure, trace the owning operation and repair the supported cause. Rerun the same path and retain a meaningful regression using the project’s runner.

request: Move our parser behind a smaller interface
decision: Pin the consumer-visible output, simplify ownership and compare the same inputs before and after. Preserve behavior and update affected callers together.

request: Reduce report generation from four seconds to two
decision: Measure a representative baseline, change one supported bottleneck and compare under similar conditions. Report variability and the observed user-facing result.

request: Why is the ownership check in the service?
decision: Inspect code, history and the actual permission boundary. Separate observed facts from inference and return the answer without starting an unrequested implementation.

request: Review this PR and repair the confirmed regression
decision: Review intent and quality, trace indirect consumers and reproduce material findings. Fix authorized defects on the existing branch and recheck the changed behavior.

request: Repair the command that opens saved items in our app
decision: Reuse the project’s actual driver and runtime. Verify checkout identity, drive the user path, inspect its result and clean up only owned resources.

request: Set up a new project; the language and test runner are fixed
decision: Honor fixed choices. Identify product constraints and the first milestone, compare open decisions, then build and verify the smallest real path using project-owned guidance.

request: Use Rust and cargo for a file converter; module boundaries are open
decision: Keep the selected language and build tools. Compare module boundaries against the input/output behavior and consumers. Use the project’s Rust guidance and run a real conversion before reporting success.

request: Use Python and the standard library for a small config CLI
decision: Honor those choices and add only what the milestone requires. Read a real configuration file, execute the CLI and inspect its actual output and a meaningful failure case.

request: Hosting is open and my usual provider may be wrong for this product
decision: Compare viable choices against execution, persistence, deployment and maintenance needs. Treat the usual provider as a preference; test relevant uncertainties and show trade-offs before committing.

request: Move this local app to the chosen cloud host
decision: Use the agreed provider and existing deployment guidance. Preserve configuration and recovery, transfer only selected data and verify the hosted path against the actual target.

request: Pay down one compiler diagnostic in our existing project
decision: Use existing check commands and project technology guidance. Fix one diagnostic without replacing tools or weakening the checks, then compare counts and finish in one PR.

request: An earlier bug report still cannot be reproduced
decision: Retain the attempts and missing information. A bug-fix loop skips a prior needs-reproduction report until new reproduction information arrives, allowing other eligible reports to progress.

request: Continue the change in our existing PR
decision: Read the current checkout, prior decisions and relevant proof. Resume the next incomplete slice in the owner-selected PR and recheck affected results.
